instructions: Discuss how far you agree or disagree with the statement. Explain your reasons, and consider ways in which the statement might or might not hold true.
Discuss how far you agree or disagree with the recommendation. Describe situations in which adopting it would or would not be wise, and explain how they shape your view.
Discuss how far you agree or disagree with the claim. In developing your position, address the strongest reasons someone might give for the opposite view.
Discuss which of the two views comes closer to your own, and explain your reasons. Address both views in your response.
Discuss how far you agree or disagree with the claim and the reason given for it.
Discuss your view of the policy and explain your reasoning. Consider the likely results of adopting it and how they shape your position.

prompts.text: Universities should require every student to take courses in subjects far outside their chosen field.
The main purpose of education is to prepare people for paid work.
Students learn more from making mistakes than from being taught the right answer.
Grades do more to discourage learning than to encourage it.
Schools should teach students how to think rather than what to think.
Some believe that teachers should be paid according to their students' test results. Others believe that test results are too narrow a measure to decide a teacher's pay.
As machines take over more tasks, people are losing skills that matter.
Governments should regulate new technologies before their effects are fully understood.
The ease of finding information online has made people less likely to think deeply.
Technological progress always creates as many problems as it solves.
Scientific research should be funded on the basis of its likely practical benefits.
The best scientists are those who question the accepted theories of their field.
Some argue that scientists have a duty to explain their work to the public. Others argue that scientists should focus on research and leave communication to others.
Researchers should share their data freely, because science advances fastest when results can be checked by anyone.
Leaders should be judged by the results they achieve rather than by the methods they use.
Governments should spend more on preventing problems than on solving them after they arise.
A society should be judged by how it treats its least powerful members.
Public officials should be required to disclose all of their financial interests.
Laws should be flexible enough to allow for exceptions in special cases.
The study of history is valuable mainly because it helps us avoid repeating past mistakes.
Popular culture tells us more about a society than its fine art does.
Cities should protect old buildings even when new ones would serve people better.
Some say that art should challenge its audience. Others say that art should comfort and delight.
Museums should return objects to the countries they were taken from.
Competition brings out the best in people.
People are more likely to change their views through personal experience than through argument.
It is more important to be kind than to be honest.
Communities should be responsible for caring for their elderly members, rather than leaving it to families alone.
The best way to understand a group of people is to study its traditions.
Success in any career depends more on persistence than on talent.
Organizations should promote employees from within rather than hire leaders from outside.
Some believe that people should choose a career they love even if it pays poorly. Others believe that financial security should come first.
Working in teams produces better results than working alone.
Individuals can do little to protect the environment; only governments and large companies can make a real difference.
Countries should be willing to slow their economic growth in order to protect the natural world.
People should pay the full cost of the resources they use, including the harm to future generations.
The most important discoveries often come from people working outside a field rather than within it.
It is better to know a little about many subjects than a great deal about one.
Questioning authority is necessary for progress.
People should be skeptical of any claim that is widely accepted, because common beliefs are often wrong.
